name: Hind Rectifiers Ltd (HIRECT)
tagline: India's pre-eminent railway traction-transformer maker (~45-50% share) migrating up to full propulsion systems, with a large Railways-electrification order book and a FY31 $1bn vision -- but Q1 FY27 standalone growth decelerated to +10% (vs a 30% guide), P/E is ~65-76x, and a loss-making France unit is dragging consolidated numbers
business_overview: Hind Rectifiers (est. 1958, originally with Westinghouse Brake & Signal UK) is India's leading domestic manufacturer of traction transformers and railway power electronics. It is transitioning from a component/sub-system supplier to a full-stack traction propulsion and power-management platform - it has started receiving Indian Railways orders for complete propulsion systems (Rs 60 Cr for 4 MEMU train sets, a Rs 60 Cr Vande Metro development order). Management guides ~30% standalone revenue growth for FY27 and beyond and has articulated a FY31 'vision' of ~$1 billion revenue. A France acquisition (CTC production) has been added and is scaling but is currently loss-making.

Revenue Rs 999.1 Cr (+52.5%), EBITDA Rs 84.1 Cr (+19.6%), PAT (after minority) ~Rs 45 Cr -- France (Elventive) dilutive
Standalone revenue Rs 236.4 Cr (+10% YoY), PAT Rs 15.1 Cr (+18%); consolidated revenue Rs 258.4 Cr (+20.3%), PAT only Rs 6.5 Cr (Elventive France loss ~Rs 6.5 Cr)
~Rs 845 Cr (Mar-2026) rising to an all-time-high ~Rs 1,099 Cr; FY26 fresh inflows Rs 858 Cr; Railways-electrification-driven

fundamentals_narrative: FY26 standalone was a genuinely strong year -- revenue +45%, PAT +55%, ROCE ~24%, operating cash flow up 2.5x to ~Rs 91 Cr -- and the migration from components/sub-systems into full traction-propulsion systems is a real step-up in content per train set, with the first Indian Railways propulsion orders (Rs 60 Cr for 4 MEMU sets + a Rs 60 Cr Vande Metro development order) already in hand. But the near-term numbers turned: Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew only ~10% YoY -- well below the 30% guidance and the FY26 base -- and consolidated PAT was just Rs 6.5 Cr because the France (Elventive) unit is loss-making (~Rs 6.5 Cr/quarter, guided 18-24 months to profitability). The stock is expensive (P/E ~65-76x, EV/EBITDA ~46x), debtor days are rising (~70 -> ~87), full propulsion-vendor approval is only targeted for end-FY27 (currently eligible for ~20% of tendered quantities), and Indian Railways is effectively a single monopsony buyer so order timing and pricing sit outside the company's control. A Rs 100 Cr preferential issue to Tata Mutual Fund funds the ~20% traction-transformer capacity expansion.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Stock ran from a ~Rs 565 52-week low to a ~Rs 1,399 high; a WebSearch-referenced 2021 episode showed the same name is capable of ~35% moves in a few days - a volatile, momentum-prone counter.
sentiment_summary: Read the full thread (8 posts of 10), Jun to Aug 2026 - a young thread. Midhunjoe's opener (9 loves) is the core bull case: pre-eminent domestic traction-transformer maker undergoing a structural transformation to a propulsion/power-management platform, strong FY26 standalone print, 30% guided growth, FY31 $1bn vision. His July 2026 follow-up flags the first propulsion-system orders from Indian Railways (Rs 60 Cr MEMU + Rs 60 Cr Vande Metro development orders) as a major value migration - once approved as a full-service propulsion vendor the run-rate should step up materially. RocketMan (4 loves) adds useful engineering context on why variable-voltage-variable-frequency traction converters are essential and hard to displace. Two counter-notes: vnktshb points out the bull is quoting standalone, not the weaker consolidated numbers; Md_Uzair (Q1 FY27) calls the quarter 'decent', noting YoY comparisons are distorted by the France acquisition and CTC production is scaling (topline doubled QoQ).

verdict_headline: Real propulsion-system value-migration story on a large Railways order book, but cut to LOW-MEDIUM conviction: Q1 FY27 standalone growth decelerated to +10%, consolidated PAT is negligible on the France drag, and the ~65-76x multiple prices the full thesis already
verdict_reasoning: The value migration into full propulsion systems is a genuine, specific catalyst with the first Indian Railways orders in hand and full-vendor approval targeted for end-FY27, on top of a strong FY26 standalone print and a large rising order book. four_box scores 3.0 (tailwind + tam + moat yes; valuation no), so the 10x-in-2-3-years label is permitted.

Conviction cut Medium -> Low-Medium: Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew only ~10% YoY (vs the 30% guide), consolidated PAT was just Rs 6.5 Cr with the France unit dragging ~Rs 6.5 Cr/quarter for another 18-24 months, and at ~65-76x the multiple needs sustained 35%+ EPS growth that the current run-rate does not support. The story is intact; the near-term numbers and the price are not aligned with it.

Red-flag check: none. Rising debtor days, the loss-making France acquisition and the aspirational FY31 vision are quality / credibility caveats that cap conviction but do not meet AVOID / HIGH CAUTION / EXCLUDE definitions.

Re-check on: (a) full-service propulsion-vendor approval vs the end-FY27 target, (b) standalone growth re-accelerating toward the 30% guide, (c) France (Elventive) turning EBITDA-positive, (d) debtor days and consolidated PAT catching up to standalone.

four_box.note: Railways electrification tailwind, propulsion-system content-migration catalyst, and a genuine engineering moat (OHE -> V/f drive, ~45-50% traction-transformer share) all score well; P/E ~65-76x / EV-EBITDA ~46x already prices the optionality -- valuation no. Score 3.0 keeps 10x-in-2-3-years permitted; conviction cut to Low-Medium because Q1 FY27 standalone growth decelerated to +10% and the loss-making France unit keeps consolidated PAT negligible.
